item.title: Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (Unemployment Labs (Will DePue))
item.description: A first-hand forensic study showing that the way PyTorch splits random weight initialisation across a GPU's processors leaves a trace of the chip in every published model, and using it to argue that six recent models from DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group began training on Nvidia Blackwell chips that cannot legally be exported to China. It explains the method, how it was validated on real H100, B300, GB200 and MI300X hardware, what the training runs likely cost, and, carefully, what the evidence does not prove. A sharp intersection of AI engineering, export controls and US-China rivalry that will be argued over for weeks.

item.title: A Strange Quantum Theorem Has Killed Einstein’s Reality (Quanta Magazine (Charlie Wood))
item.description: Traces the argument over whether the quantum state describes reality itself or only our knowledge of it, from Einstein's 1935 objection and Bell's 1964 theorem to the 2012 PBR theorem, which rules out the comfortable middle ground in which the wavefunction is mere information about an objective world. Recent tests, including one run on an IBM quantum computer, back the theorem, leaving physicists to choose between a strange objective reality and none at all. A clear 'aha' about what quantum mechanics actually forbids, told through the people who proved it.

item.title: Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026 (METR)
item.description: The first outside audit of whether a frontier lab is using its own AI to speed up AI research. With staff interviews, surveys and Anthropic's internal benchmark index, METR estimates Anthropic now improves its models on well-specified tasks about twice as fast as in 2024-25 (plausibly 1.3x to 3x), finds that training compute growth did not accelerate, and judges that about 80 percent of the speed-up comes from AI itself. It is also candid about the limits: Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR found most informative. A first-hand look at the mechanics behind the 'recursive self-improvement' talking point.
